OTA-1875 — the list gets its scroll back

The owner opened the Fusing Crucible on a Pixel 10 Pro XL, reached the
upgrade-target stage, and the surface went dead. His words are the reason this
was findable at all:

    "It's not the push alone, even the scroll froze.
     Nothing on the screen except the cancel reacted."

THREE SYMPTOMS AND ONE NON-SYMPTOM, ALL FROM ONE STRUCTURE. The card sat inside a
second `TouchableWithoutFeedback` whose only job was `onPress={() => {}}` — a
swallow, so a tap on the card would not reach the outer scrim's dismiss. A
Touchable attaches its responder handlers to its ONE CHILD, so that swallow put
`onStartShouldSetResponder` on the card — an ANCESTOR of the ScrollView — and a
descendant cannot take the responder back from an ancestor:

    scroll dead        the pan never reached the ScrollView
    blocked rows dead  they are <View>, not controls, so nothing deeper claimed
                       the touch and it died on the swallow's empty handler
    Cancel ALIVE       a Pressable DOES win first claim, and it sits outside the
                       list

The fourth observation is the one that made it provable rather than plausible: a
global input, presentation or JS fault cannot spare one control and kill only its
sibling subtree.

THE OUTER TOUCHABLE WAS THE SAME HAZARD, one level up — it wrapped the backdrop,
which is also an ancestor of the card — so removing only the inner swallow would
have moved the claim rather than removed it. The scrim is now a Pressable SIBLING
rendered behind the card: taps outside it dismiss, taps on the card reach the
card's own subtree, and nothing that can claim the responder sits above the list.

AND THE SURFACE CAN NOW BE READ. FusionPickerModal carried NONE of the
touch/presentation instrument — it was the one modal outside the seam, which is
why the incident ring showed a finger arriving and then said nothing at all about
what it reached. It now speaks the vocabulary CrucibleGuardModal already speaks:
`pres` mount/unmount, a capture-phase `modal` observer that returns false and
never claims, and in → enter → dispatch → done on the scrim, the rows, the
catalyst, Back, Cancel and confirm. NO per-scroll or per-frame diagnostic — the
256-entry ring has to survive the recurrence, not drown in it.

TRANSACTION: NO CHANGE, RULING C. The incident's `−25 TC` looked like a loss and
is not one. It buys a PERMIT (`fusionPending`), granted in the same `set()` as
the charge, which survives saves by design and is cleared ONLY inside the single
atomic `set()` that also delivers the fused item (craftingSlice) or the upgrade
(gameStore). There is no window where the permit clears without the goods, so no
resource-loss path exists to repair and the economics are untouched.

BLOCKED ROWS UNTOUCHED, by owner ruling: they stay non-actionable with their
existing explanatory copy. This gives the list its scroll back; it does not turn
a refusal into a control.

THE REGRESSION IS STRUCTURAL, AND §D IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. §A reads the
source, which a later pass could satisfy by moving the Touchable elsewhere. §D
mounts the real component and walks UPWARD from the real ScrollView, asserting no
Touchable ancestor and no start-responder ancestor. Restoring the swallow turns
four tests red, including both tree rules.

⚠ CrucibleGuardModal carries the same shape and is DELIBERATELY NOT REPAIRED
here — owner scope: "I do not want to alter another responder surface while
repairing the one we are investigating." It is allowlisted BY NAME, and a test
asserts the allowlist entry is not vacuous, so if anyone repairs it the rule
fails until the entry is deleted. A named debt, not a silent one.

⚠ NOT CLAIMED: that the freeze is cured on hardware. The structural defect is
proven in the component and it explains every discriminator the owner reported,
and the physical incident is strongly consistent with it — but no physical
post-repair verification has happened and none is claimed here.
